note:
# Census pass: P-E-2019-1902029-f44b44ca

## What the paper is
An ecosystem service value (ESV) model in the Costanza lineage: a per-hectare value
coefficient per land type, times area, aggregated to a total, applied to fourteen Chinese
provinces, then to two projects - the Yangtze River Delta and the Huangguoshu scenic area -
and finally folded into a multi-objective nonlinear program that scores land-use plans.
Twenty-eight physical pages, twenty-five printed exhibits: twenty-three "figures" and two
"Tables".

## Coverage arithmetic
Twenty-five measured regions on sixteen of the twenty-eight pages, and they close with
nothing left over: twenty-three figure rows plus two table rows, zero exclusions, zero
unaccounted. That makes it the first paper in the lane with no excluded region at all - every display equation in this paper is live vector text, so unlike #169,
#170 and most of the lane there is no equation image for the region pass to box and then
throw away.

## The finding: eleven of the twenty-three figures are grids
This is the paper that breaks the exhibit census open. Figures 2, 3, 6, 10 and 17 to 23 all
print numbers in a ruled matrix, and all eleven wear figure captions; the only two objects
called "Table" are, at 2x6 and 10x2, the two smallest grids in the document. So a paper
that counts "figures" and "tables" from its own captions reports 23 and 2, and a census
that counts what is actually printed on the page reports 12 drawings and 13 grids. The
mislabelling also runs the other way exactly once: Figure 16 is captioned "The table of
Different ecosystem importance levels" and is a six-series line chart.

The two real tables are also the two best-behaved grids: booktabs, no verticals, no zebra,
no merged cells, and four caption-above placements. The figure-captioned grids are the
ones with Excel's full box, merged tiered headers and band fills. Rule style here tracks
what the object is CALLED, not how the data sits - which is the cleanest evidence yet that
the dressing is chosen by whoever pasted the object in, not by the author's own geometry.

## Captions: twenty-five labels, no verbs, one split
Every caption prints below its exhibit except the two table captions, which print above -
the same figure/table split #167 showed, in a document where eleven of the "figures" are
grids. All twenty-five are noun phrases or stubs: no caption states a conclusion, a
condition, the method or a unit (two units, both in brackets). They are also the shortest
in the lane, five to fourteen words.

The caption text itself is damaged in three ways worth recording, because they are the
reason three rows are typed-from-crop: Figure 10's caption is truncated at the page margin
("...in Huangguossh"), Figure 9's splits "E-" / "cosystems", and Figures 13 and 14 collide
on one shared line so that the left caption is hyphenated across the page ("in Hei-" /
"longjiang").

## Citation: eight named, seventeen by deixis or not at all
Only figures 1, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 15 are ever numbered in the prose, and neither
table is. The whole appendix - seven exhibits across three pages - is never named by
number anywhere; the body sends the reader to "the appendix" three times and names no
exhibit. Pointers that do exist are unusually explicit about the act of plotting ("to get
a scatter plot in figure 4", "the radar map is drawn in figure 9"), and one sentence
introduces two exhibits at once ("As shows in figure 11 and figure 12:").

## Geometry: no panels, no depth, colour as the only key
Not one exhibit is multipanel, shares an axis, carries a colourbar or is three-dimensional.
The paper's one genuinely two-part idea - the cost-benefit argument with and without the
ecological cost - is drawn as two separate figures side by side rather than as one exhibit
with panels (a) and (b), which is why the census counts two exhibits where a better-made
paper would count one. Colour is a data channel three times (Figure 1's hierarchy levels,
Figure 6's five ESC bands, Figure 2's header tiers) and never decodes to a value.

The tick-number discipline is the weakest part: of the twelve drawings, only Figures 4,
8, 15 and 16 print both axes, Figure 14 prints an x axis beside two in-plot annotations,
and four exhibits print no number at all (Figures 1, 11, 12, 13), so the slopes and
crossings the prose reasons about in 5.2.1 are drawn shapes the reader must take on trust.

## The layer's own defects
The text layer drops the fi ligature throughout ("ﬁgure", "ﬁgure15", "Cost-beneﬁt",
"Coefﬁcient"), so every pointer quote has to be transcribed with the ligature intact, and
the prose welds a caption into a body clause ("Figure 6: Ecological service capability
classiﬁcation for people to live"). Every appendix grid pads each numeric cell with a
trailing full stop ("599.29."), which is why the decimal alignment is perfect and the
right edges are ragged. The running head reads "Team # 1902029" and "Page N of 25" across
28 physical pages, is real text rather than a raster, and is the one piece of apparatus in
this document that the region pass correctly ignores.
rules: Twenty-five measured regions, twenty-five printed exhibits, zero exclusions and zero unaccounted - the first paper in this lane with NO non-exhibit region at all, because every display equation here is live vector text and never becomes a picture [place.section_path].

ELEVEN OF THE TWENTY-THREE FIGURES ARE GRIDS DRAWN AS PICTURES: Figures 2, 3, 6, 10, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 all print numbers in a ruled matrix and all wear a figure caption, while the two objects actually called 'Table' are the two smallest grids in the document [geometry.family].

The mislabelling runs both ways once: Figure 16 is captioned 'The table of Different ecosystem importance levels' and is a six-series line chart, in a section whose prose says 'obtain the importance level table' [caption.verbatim].
Family mix of the twenty-three figures: table-as-figure 11, line 7, bar 2, scatter 1, flowchart-or-schematic 1, and one radar that still has no vocabulary word [geometry.family].

Not one of the twenty-five exhibits is multipanel, shares an axis, carries a colourbar or is three-dimensional; the paper's one two-part idea (Figures 11 and 12, the cost-benefit argument) is drawn as two separate figures side by side rather than as one exhibit with panels (a) and (b) [geometry.panel_count].

Colour is a data channel in three places and a decoration in none: Figure 1 encodes hierarchy level by box fill and prints no key, Figure 6 encodes its five ESC bands as row fills, and Figure 2 uses band fills to separate header tiers [geometry.legend].

Legends are outside or below when they exist at all: below the plot three times (Figures 8, 13, 14), right of the frame once (Figure 15, fourteen entries), above the plot once (Figure 16), and absent from the other eighteen, where the curves, bars or cells carry their own labels or - in Figures 11 and 12 - every line is labelled in place [geometry.legend].

Nineteen of the twenty-three figures print numbers and four print none at all (Figures 1, 11, 12, 13); of the seven line charts, Figures 4, 8, 15 and 16 print both axes, Figure 14 prints only its x axis beside two in-plot annotations, and the rest carry no scale, so the slope comparisons the prose draws in 5.2.1 are unchecked shapes [geometry.printed_numbers].

Every caption in the paper prints BELOW its exhibit except the two table captions, which print ABOVE the grid - the same clean figure/table split as #167, in a document where eleven of the 'figures' are grids [caption.position].

The caption form is `Figure <n>: <label>` / `Table <n>: <label>` with a colon, a lower-case or capitalised label, no terminal period except Figure 1's, and five to fourteen words - three to four times shorter than #169's sentence captions [caption.numbering].

NOT ONE CAPTION CONTAINS A FINITE VERB ABOUT ITS OWN OBJECT: all twenty-five are noun phrases or stubs ('Cost-beneﬁt curve(a)', 'Rate of Decline of Three Values', 'the impact of area change in Heilongjiang'), so no caption states a conclusion, a condition or a method, and voice is unassignable throughout [caption.voice].

Only two captions give a unit ('the ESV of 14 provinces in China (Billion yuan)', 'Ecosystem Service Value(yuan/hm2)'), and the printed grids mostly carry their unit in a stub row or a second header line instead ('Million Yuan', 'Ecological Value per Unit Area (yuan/hm^2 a)') [caption.units].

Caption text breaks at the page margin and inside words: Figure 10's caption is truncated in the print ('...in Huangguossh'), Figure 9's splits 'E-' / 'cosystems', and Figures 13 and 14 collide on one line so that the first caption is hyphenated across 'Hei-' / 'longjiang' - both typed from the crop as a result [caption.verbatim].

Eight of the twenty-three figures are ever numbered in the prose (1, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15) and NEITHER table is: the other fifteen figures and both grids are pointed at, if at all, by deixis ('The ﬁgure shows that...', 'obtain the importance level table', 'The calculation results are shown in the appendix') [mention.first_page].

The whole appendix (Figures 17 to 23, seven exhibits) is never referred to by number anywhere - the body sends the reader to 'the appendix' three times and names no exhibit, so a reader hunting Figure 20 has to page through all of section 8 [mention.count].

Pointer style is direct naming where it exists: 'Compare our calculation results with authoritative data to get a scatter plot in ﬁgure 4', 'As shows in ﬁgure 11 and ﬁgure 12:', '(see in ﬁgure 10)' - one sentence introduces two exhibits at once, Figures 11 and 12 together [mention.lead_pattern].
Lead timing is same-page or one page early and never later: Figure 4 is named on p11 and drawn on p12, every other pointer names its exhibit on the exhibit's own page [mention.lead_pages].

The reading sentence comes immediately and states a comparison or a direction, not a number: 'the indirect value and the existence value of environmental degradation are reduced at a faster rate', 'with July as the highest point, gradually decreasing to the adjacent months on both sides' [mention.trail_sentence].

The exhibits are allocated by stage: notation takes Table 1 (1.3), the model takes the flowchart and the equivalents matrix (3.3.2, 3.3.3), the calculation takes the province table and the consistency scatter (3.5.1, 3.5.2), the evaluation takes the three-chart page (3.5.3), each project takes its value table and its advice charts, and the appendix absorbs seven exhibits in three pages [place.section_kind].

One page carries three exhibits (p13: Figures 5, 6 and 7) and five pages carry two; no exhibit owns a page, no exhibit is landscape, and the largest single region is 0.1664 of a page (Figure 15) while the smallest is 0.0311 (Figure 8) [place.area_frac].

Two region areas are floors rather than measurements: Table 2 returns 0.0333 because the pass boxes only a 41-point band of a 130-point table, and Figure 8 returns 0.0311 for a chart drawn at half measure in the page's outer column [place.area_frac].

Document order equals number order throughout, so the numbering is sound even though the naming is not - the failure here is that fifteen of twenty-five exhibits are never named, not that they are named out of order [place.doc_order].

The two real grids are both booktabs with no verticals, no zebra, no merged cells, no diagonal header and no note line; the grids that wear figure captions are the ones with Excel's full box and merged headers (Figures 2, 10, 17, 18, 19, 20, 22, 23), so rule style tracks what the object is CALLED rather than how it is drawn [table.rule_style].

Decimal alignment tracks the tool, not the data: every grid whose cells were produced by the setter aligns on the point and pads each cell with a trailing full stop ('599.29.', '0.40621.'), while Table 2 - typed by hand - leaves one cell at a single decimal place beside five at two [table.decimal_aligned].

Ligature loss and welds: the text layer returns 'ﬁgure' for figure throughout, so every pointer quote has to be transcribed with the ligature intact, and the prose welds 'ﬁgure15' with no space while the caption welds a body clause onto Figure 6's label ('...classiﬁcation for people to live') [mention.style].

tables.note: One header row and one data row: the adjusted per-hectare value of six land types for the delta (37979.23 / 12584.42 / 12000.82 / 108001.3 / 79956.43 / 734.44), unit only in the caption ('yuan/hm2'), rule above the header, under it and under the row, no verticals, no zebra, no decimals aligned - one cell runs to a single decimal place where its neighbours run to two. It is the paper's smallest grid at half measure and the layout pass boxes only a 41-point band of it, so the recorded area 0.0333 is a floor: the printed table runs from about 572 to 703 pt while the pass returns 618 to 659.
